title: Sánchez’s gamble: This ‘all-in’ election will have international impact
gist: Chatham House argues Sánchez's snap election, called after a housing bill failed, is a high-risk bet that hinges on uniting a fragmented left, and kicks off a year of polarized European elections that could hamper EU defense coordination.

insights.claim: Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez called a snap election after Parliament rejected emergency housing legislation amid affordability protests, though one was legally due by August 2027 and his coalition has not passed a full budget since 2023.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Spanish political risk rises; watch the roughly 50-day campaign.

insights.claim: Sánchez is vulnerable on multiple fronts: the January decree regularizing 500,000 undocumented migrants, the July Ceuta surge, worsening housing affordability, the Koldo corruption case and the charging of his wife with embezzlement and corruption.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Each is a lever for opposition on both flanks.

insights.claim: Sánchez will repeat his 2023 playbook of framing a binary choice between Sanchismo and a backward-looking far right, using Trump, Milei and Flávio Bolsonaro as foils.
insights.speaker: Chatham House

insights.claim: Spain's D'Hondt system punishes parties polling in low single figures, so unity on the left (Sumar's 'Frente Amplio', possibly led by Gabriel Rufián) matters more than ever, but Spanish left pacts often collapse, as Podemos left Sumar's list within months of 2023.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Left unification success is the swing factor for seat count.

insights.claim: The right's Partido Popular is expected to run a 'Ming Vase strategy' of avoiding mishaps, but leader Alberto Feijóo's inability to answer questions about a Vox coalition likely cost him victory in 2023.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: A PP-Vox coalition question could again dominate.

insights.claim: Spain begins a year of polarized European elections, with France choosing a president in spring 2027 and Italy, Poland, Finland and Greece also due to vote, many featuring fragile left coalitions facing a surging right.
insights.speaker: Chatham House

insights.claim: Disruptive elections will make it harder to build a more coherent joint European approach to security as the US presses Europe to do more for its own defence.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Slower EU defense integration; relevant to defense spending themes.
